title: Numerical recovery of point orders from common divisor thresholds
statement: Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and let $E$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] transverse to $N$ (its local equations restrict to distinct coordinate parameters on $N$). Let $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ be coherent and $d\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q\ge0:I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with value $\infty$ for zero, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(I,d)=\{x:\operatorname{ord}_xI\ge d\}$. A test transformation is an open restriction, a smooth-center blowup in cosupport with normal crossings with $E$, a product with a line adjoining its zero section to $E$, or a blowup of the intersection of two boundary hypersurfaces. For a cosupport blowup use the strict transform of $N$ and the ideal $e^{-d}\sigma^*I$, where $e$ is the exceptional equation; for the last two operations use ordinary pullback. Two such data on the same ambient scheme and with the same ordered boundary are test equivalent if their finite test sequences coincide. Let $(N,I,d)$ and $(P,J,b)$ be test equivalent, where $P$ is also smooth and has the same local dimension as $N$.  After any common finite sequence [def-trf-common-marked-test-sequence], write $(T,M_T,P_T)$ for its endpoints, $d_T,b_T$ for their marks, and take arbitrary support points $x\in M_T$, $y\in P_T$ with the same ambient image in both cosupports. Then $\operatorname{ord}_x I_T\,b_T=\operatorname{ord}_y J_T\,d_T$ in $\mathbb N_\infty$. No boundary-order equality is asserted.

proof.text: Membership of the image point in cosupport gives m>=d and n>=b: the support embedding is injective, so the witnessing cosupport point is the specified one. Apply the cylinder threshold comparison for every k>=1 and i>=0.

proof.text: If just m is infinite and n is finite, use k=1 and i=n. Success on the infinite side implies (n+2)b<=n, contradicting b>=1. The symmetric case is identical. If both are infinite then positive finite marks preserve infinity.

proof.text: For finite m,n, suppose nd<mb. Let k=db and i=nd-db, which is nonnegative since n>=b. Then k+i+1=nd+1. Multiplying nd+1<=mb by d gives the first success inequality. The corresponding second inequality would say (nd+1)b<=dbn=ndb, impossible since b>0. Interchanging the two data rules out mb<nd. Hence mb=nd. This exact separation replaces the supremum approximation of original step 7.

lean.statement: theorem test_sequence_point_order_recovery (S : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (M P : Marked S) [LocallyOfFiniteType S.p] [QuasiCompact S.p] (hboundary : IsStrictNormalCrossingsBoundary (⨅ i : Fin S.boundary.length, S.boundary.get i)) (hordered : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : S.Z.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ S.boundary.get i)) (hM : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : M.N.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ (S.boundary.get i).comap M.j)) (hP : HasAdaptedNormalCrossingsCenter (⊥ : P.N.IdealSheafData) (fun i ↦ (S.boundary.get i).comap P.j)) (hdim : ∀ (x : M.N) (y : P.N), M.j x = P.j y → ringKrullDim (M.N.presheaf.stalk x) = ringKrullDim (P.N.presheaf.stalk y)) (hequivalent : RestrictedEquivalent M P) : ∀ (T : Embedded (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (M' P' : Marked T), CommonTestSequence M P M' P' → ∀ (x : M'.N) (y : P'.N), M'.j x = P'.j y → M'.j x ∈ M'.cosupport → P'.j y ∈ P'.cosupport → order M'.ideal x * (P'.marking : ℕ∞) = order P'.ideal y * (M'.marking : ℕ∞)
